# Badge

A short label for a status, category or count, next to what it describes.

**In Content first.** The topic of an article.

## See it live

<div class="odv-live"><span class="odv-wait">Start Storybook to see it live: <code>npm run storybook</code></span><iframe src="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-badge--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:content-first" title="Badge examples in Storybook" loading="lazy"></iframe><div class="bar"><span>Live from Storybook</span><a href="http://localhost:6006/?path=/docs/components-badge--docs">Open Badge in Storybook</a><a href="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-badge--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:content-first;mode:dark">See it in dark</a></div></div>

## When to use it

- **Use it when:** A state people scan for in a list or table, or a small category label.
- **Not when:** A message people must read (alert or toast), or an action (a button).

Instead:

- [Alert](./alert.md): A message, not a label.
- [Button](./button.md): Something to press.

## How Content first uses it

<div class="odv-grid two"><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">A status</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Badge pill with a word</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> An icon alone</div></div><div class="cap">Status is rare; a word is clear.</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">Shape of a status badge</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> radius.badge (pill)</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> A rectangle</div></div><div class="cap">Pills sit softly next to text.</div></div></div>

## Why it works this way

Badge looks the way it does because of 2 answers about this product. Each card is one answer, in three steps: the answer, what it decided for Badge, and what would move if it changed.

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-accessibility-count"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How many signals carry each meaning?</b><code>accessibility.count</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Two: color and word</div><p>Status is rare; color and a word are enough.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Badge</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>neutral</b>: Saved: waiting for you; nothing is wrong.</span></li><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>info</b>: Topics and reading states need no news tone; status is rare.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>success</b>: Finished: you read it to the end.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>warning</b>: Out of date: the facts may have changed since it was written.</span></li><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>danger</b>: Nothing in an article fails; errors are calm sentences, not labels.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Alert: destructive</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">5</div><small>Badge decisions would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-voice-count"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How many tones does it use?</b><code>voice.count</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">One per moment</div><p>Warm by default, calmer for errors.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Badge</h5><ul><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>danger</b>: Nothing in an article fails; errors are calm sentences, not labels.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Alert: destructive</code> <code>Toast: danger</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Badge decision would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

## Words

- Write to one person: "you", not "users".
- Short sentences with room to breathe.
- Explain why before asking for anything.
- Use: Read, Save for later, You, Next issue. Avoid: Click here, Submit, Users, Content.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Not now
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Browse guides

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

Test before you ship:

- [ ] The status is a word; color and icon add to it, never replace it. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add badge
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Component keys

The CSS variable is the key with `/` replaced by `-` and the base `@` dropped. Each key points to a token; values live only on primitives.

| Key | What it controls | Points to, light | Points to, dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `badge/radius` | Badge corner radius. | `radius.badge` → `content-first.theme.base.radius.badge` → `radius.999` | same |
| `badge/padding-x` | Horizontal padding inside a badge. | `space.gap.tight` → `space.8` | same |
| `badge/font-size` | Badge label size. | `type.caption.font-size` → `font.size.14` | same |
| `badge/neutral/background` | Neutral badge fill. | `color.surface.sunken` → `content-first.theme.light.color.surface.sunken` → `color.stone.light.100` | `color.surface.sunken` → `content-first.theme.dark.color.surface.sunken` → `color.stone.dark.100` |
| `badge/neutral/label` | Neutral badge label. | `color.text.secondary` → `content-first.theme.light.color.text.secondary` → `color.stone.light.700` | `color.text.secondary` → `content-first.theme.dark.color.text.secondary` → `color.stone.dark.500` |
